The worst case is documented as 210 s plus queue wait. Tests default_timeouts_which_resend and timeout_then_budget_ends_with_timeout cover it. Residual: I could not read the omitted-long lines 279 and 283, so I did not confirm that the duplicate-POST and billing risk is stated in the text.

a-5 line 173 and A5-23: request is one global deadline (ureq timeout_global). Timeouts::probe() (5 s / 10 s) is used for discover, models and doctor. Worst-case wall clock is documented (line 281). See new RSH-013 for the remaining per-runner knob.

a-5 lines 48, 245-273, A5-03 and A5-21: ProviderPause is shared per host across clones. Retry-After is clamped to 250 ms-30 s with 0-250 ms jitter. Tests cover retry_after_zero_floored, pause_is_per_host and pause_shared_by_clones.
a-10 lines 52, 58, 237-247, 523: decide::signal uses ctrlc (termination feature) to cancel the token. Unfinished requests end decision.cancelled, flush_session_log runs, and the exit code is 130.
a-10 lines 59, 431, 489, 524: recv_timeout(100 ms) then py.check_signals() with the GIL. KeyboardInterrupt or an on_result exception cancels the token, drains, and re-raises. Python test 6 covers it.

a-9 line 265 and test drop_mid_batch_one_row_per_started_job (line 232): Drop cancels the JobQueue, never the caller's token, joins no thread, bounds a lingering worker by the request deadline, and writes one row per submitted job.
a-4 lines 141-152, 216, 314: MAX_WORKERS 64 and MAX_MAX_SENDS 10 are checked at load as config.invalid with the key path. a-9 uses checked arithmetic for queue_capacity.
a-4 lines 164-200, 255, 314-315: RunnerHost, RunnerKind, NonZeroU16 port and VarName key_env are validated at load. A key_env on a non-loopback host is config.key_on_plain_http.
a-8 lines 157-179, 294: LogContext supplies session_id and position and sets correlation_id. a-9 line 235 test busy_records_carry_session and line 267 cover it.
a-5 A5-15 adds elapsed_ms. a-9 line 137 uses try_write (never blocks) on the cancel, orphan and abandon paths.
a-9 line 266: the result queue is bounded at queue_capacity and a worker blocks on a full queue. Test slow_consumer_blocks_workers.

a-10 lines 150-153 and 84: MAX_REQUEST_BYTES 8 MiB, MAX_BATCH_LINES 10,000, MAX_BATCH_BYTES 256 MiB, MAX_IMAGE_BYTES 20 MiB, all with typed LimitExceeded. a-2 line 200 adds MAX_IMAGES 20. REQ-SAG-0014 is covered. The 8 MiB response cap still bounds text kept whole in session rows.

findings.issue: Timeouts stays code-level: every send uses 10 s connect / 120 s request, with no per-runner or per-provider knob. A local runner that loads a checkpoint on demand (Laya, a-6) can exceed 120 s on its first call. Because of the 90 s start budget and max_sends, the timed-out request is resent at most a few times and then fails. An operator has no setting to change this.
findings.recommendation: Either add an optional request_timeout_secs per local_runners entry, validated at load with a minimum and a maximum, or record in the plan that 120 s is a deliberate fixed ceiling and the cold-start failure is accepted.
